# Privacy Policy Template for Sealmetrics Clients

> The Spanish version is the reference text; this English version is provided for convenience.

**Document for:** Sealmetrics clients (data controllers)
**Purpose:** Model wording for the analytics section of the privacy policy of the client's website (clause 5.1 of the DPA)
**Version:** 3.0 (2026-09-24)
**Note:** Guidance only, not legal advice. The technical description of the processing is Sealmetrics' responsibility (clause 3.6 of the DPA). The legal adaptation to your case and its publication are the client's responsibility, to be carried out with its legal counsel.

---

## Why you need to update your policy

As a Sealmetrics client, you are the **Controller** of the data of your website's visitors. Sealmetrics acts as your **Processor** under the DPA. Informing your visitors (Arts. 12 and 13 GDPR) is **your** obligation, and supervisory authorities review it with particular attention:

- The **AEPD guidance on audience measurement** (January 2024, section III.A.1) requires you to inform about the use of these tools **in your privacy policy**.
- The **EDPB Guidelines 04/2026** on fines (Example 9) describe an infringement of Arts. 12 and 13: the privacy policy presented as "anonymous" data that was in fact **pseudonymised**. It was treated as a minor infringement only because the controller corrected it promptly.
- According to those same Guidelines, the controller is also liable for infringements its processor commits on its behalf (§42). An accurate description protects both of you.

That is why this version 3.0 **no longer uses the word "anonymous"** for the data Sealmetrics processes. It describes what actually happens: a **pseudonymised, ephemeral, non-persistent identifier** and **aggregated reports**.

---

## Five rules before copying

1. **Do not say the data is "anonymous"** or that "no personal data is processed". The session identifier is a pseudonym and, while it exists, it is personal data. Use the wording in this template.
2. **Include the blocks that match your configuration.** Block A is mandatory. Blocks B to F depend on what you have enabled. In the dashboard, **Settings › Privacy** shows which blocks apply to you.
3. **Do not send personal data through properties, URLs or campaign names**: emails, phone numbers, names, ID numbers, customer IDs, etc. Clause 5.2 of the DPA prohibits it. If you do, your policy will be incomplete.
4. **Sealmetrics does not use cookies or store anything on the device**, so there is nothing to declare in your cookie table. Whether you need a banner is a separate question: measurement relies on the audience-measurement exemption, which each national authority interprets. If your website targets Germany or Italy, which apply stricter criteria, check with your legal counsel.
5. **Keep the text up to date.** If Sealmetrics notifies you of a change to the processing or a new version of this template, update your policy within 30 days (clause 5.1 of the DPA).

### Block A — Audience measurement (mandatory)

#### Web analytics

To understand how this site is used and improve it, we use **Sealmetrics**, a European audience-measurement tool that acts as our data processor.

**How it works.** Sealmetrics **does not set cookies or store information on your device** (nor in localStorage, sessionStorage or other browser storage). To count visits without storing anything on your device:

- When you load a page, the measurement code **reads some technical characteristics of your browser**: browser type, language, time zone, screen resolution and similar. From them it computes, **on the fly**, a technical session identifier.
- That identifier **is pseudonymised on Sealmetrics' servers** using a secret key and a random value that **is destroyed every day**. It cannot be used to recognise you from one day to the next or across different websites.
- **No visitor profiles are created** and you are not followed across other websites.

**Data processed**

| Data | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Technical session identifier | Ephemeral pseudonym computed from technical characteristics of the browser. It is not stored on your device and changes every day |
| Pages visited | Which pages you view, in what order, which page you came from and the approximate duration of the visit |
| Visit source | How you arrived: search engine, link, social network or campaign (UTM parameters) |
| Device | Device type, browser and operating system. The full text that identifies your browser (the "user agent") is not retained; only these categories |
| Country | Approximate country, **derived from your browser's time zone**, not from your IP address |
| Interactions | Actions on the site, such as clicks or form submissions, that we have configured as events |

Your **IP address** reaches the servers with each request, as with any internet connection. Sealmetrics uses it transiently to filter abusive traffic and **does not store it in its analytics database**.

**Purpose and legal basis.** The sole purpose is **audience measurement**: statistics on the use of the site. There are two bases:

- **Reading of browser characteristics.** It relies on the consent exemption for audience-measurement tools recognised by the AEPD (January 2024 guidance) and other European authorities, because it is used solely to produce statistics for us.
- **Processing of the data.** It is based on our **legitimate interest** in understanding the aggregated use of the site (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

**Retention**

| Data | Period |
|------|--------|
| State of the ongoing session | 2 hours |
| Random value that pseudonymises the identifier | 24 hours; then destroyed |
| Technical log of each event | 1 day |
| Hourly aggregated statistics | 90 days |
| Daily aggregated statistics | 24 months |

**Where it is processed.** All measurement data is processed and stored in the **European Union**. It is not transferred outside the European Economic Area.

**Recipients.** Sealmetrics S.L. (Spain), as data processor, and its hosting sub-processors in the EU. The list is available at https://sealmetrics.com/dpa. We do not disclose this data to third parties or use it for advertising purposes.

**Your rights.** You may exercise your rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction and **objection**. To do so:

- Write to us at `[site privacy email]`.
- If you contact Sealmetrics (privacy@sealmetrics.com), it will forward your request to us.

Please note that the identifier is ephemeral and does not contain your name or contact details. For that reason, we will normally **not be able to locate the specific data of your visit** (Art. 11 GDPR), unless you provide information that makes it possible.

`[If your site offers a mechanism to opt out of measurement, state it here: "You can opt out of measurement at [link]".]`

You may also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (in Spain, the Agencia Española de Protección de Datos, www.aepd.es).

### Block B — Conversion attribution (if you measure conversions or sales)

#### Conversion measurement

When you perform an action we consider a conversion (for example `[a purchase, a sign-up or an information request]`), Sealmetrics records:

- the type of conversion;
- the amount, if any;
- the order characteristics we have configured (`[e.g. product category, number of items]`);
- the source of the visit that led to it.

If you arrived from an ad, the campaign click identifier (for example `gclid` or `fbclid`) is used **transiently** to attribute the conversion to the right campaign. **That identifier is not stored**: only the type of ad network is kept.

The purpose is to understand which channels and campaigns generate results. The basis is our **legitimate interest** (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR), which we have balanced against your rights. Conversions and their characteristics are retained for **24 months**. We do not include your name, email or other contact details in this measurement.

---

### Block C — Shopify stores (if you use the Sealmetrics Shopify integration)

#### Order attribution in the store

To attribute your purchases to the visit that led to them, Sealmetrics adds **technical data** to your cart: the technical session identifier (the one described in Block A), a reference to our account, your browser's time zone and the time. This data becomes associated with the order in our store and is sent to Sealmetrics when the order is completed.

Legal basis: our **legitimate interest** in measuring the performance of our campaigns (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). It is not used for any other purpose.

---

### Block D — Automated-traffic detection (only if you have it enabled)

#### Detection of bots and automated agents

To distinguish human visits from automated traffic (bots, automated browsers and AI agents) and prevent it from distorting our statistics, Sealmetrics analyses:

- additional technical browser signals (graphics capabilities such as WebGL or canvas, plugins, window size);
- interaction patterns (mouse movements, scrolling and click speed);
- and, transiently, your **IP address**, to derive the country and network provider.

These signals are used **only** to classify the visit as human or automated. They are not used to identify you or for any other purpose, and the IP is not stored.

The basis is our **legitimate interest** in the integrity of our statistics (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). You may object as described in Block A.

---

### Block E — Analysis with artificial intelligence (if you use Lens / Seal AI)

#### Automated analysis of statistics

We may use the Sealmetrics artificial intelligence assistant to analyse our usage statistics. The AI works on the **analytics reports**: aggregated figures and breakdowns by page, source, country, device or conversion characteristics. It does not create visitor profiles or make decisions that affect you.

The default provider ("Seal AI") processes the information **in the European Union** (Scaleway, France) and does not use it to train models.

`[If you connect your own key from another AI provider (BYOK), replace the previous paragraph: "We use [provider], which acts as our processor; [location and transfer safeguards]".]`

> Use it at most as a summary linked to the full text. A short version must still provide the essential information required by Art. 13.

### Web analytics

We use **Sealmetrics**, a European audience-measurement tool, as our data processor. **It does not set cookies or store anything on your device.** To count visits, it reads technical characteristics of your browser and computes a **pseudonymised session identifier that changes every day**: it does not allow you to be recognised from one day to the next or on other sites.

It processes:
- the pages visited;
- the source of the visit;
- the device type;
- the country (derived from the time zone, not from the IP)`[; and conversions and their origin]`.

The IP is not stored in the analytics database. The purpose is audience measurement and the basis is our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). The technical log is kept for 1 day and aggregated statistics for 24 months. Everything is processed in the EU.

You may object and exercise your other rights at `[email]`. More information at `[link to the full section]`.

## What not to write

| Do not write | Write |
|----------------|---------|
| "The data is anonymous" / "anonymous analytics" | "pseudonymised, ephemeral identifier" / "aggregated statistics" |
| "We do not process personal data" / "the GDPR does not apply" | "minimal pseudonymised processing, without identifying or following you" |
| "No fingerprinting" | "computes on the fly an identifier from technical characteristics of the browser, which changes every day" |
| "We do not collect your IP" | "the IP is not stored in the analytics database" |
| "We do not need your consent" (as a general statement) | "relies on the audience-measurement exemption" |
| "Sealmetrics is approved / certified by the AEPD or the CNIL" | Nothing: no authority certifies tools |

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Do I need to ask for consent to use Sealmetrics?

For audience measurement, Sealmetrics is designed to operate **under the audience-measurement exemption**. This exemption is recognised by the AEPD (January 2024 guidance), the CNIL and other authorities for tools that meet their criteria:

- purpose limited to statistics;
- processing solely for the publisher;
- no cross-site tracking;
- limited retention.

The exemption is **national**: each authority sets its own criteria, and Germany and Italy are stricter. The final decision about your website is yours. Sealmetrics provides its assessment against the AEPD criteria (privacy@sealmetrics.com) so that your legal counsel can evaluate it.

### Why doesn't it say "anonymous" any more?

Because it would not be accurate. The session identifier is a **pseudonym**: it does not contain your name, it rotates every day and it is signed with a secret key. Even so, technically it allows one visit to be distinguished from another during its short life. According to the EDPB, pseudonymised data is still personal data. Calling it "anonymous" in your policy is precisely the mistake that authorities sanction as a lack of transparency.

### Do I have to add Sealmetrics to the cookie banner?

There is no Sealmetrics cookie to declare. If your consent management platform (CMP) scans the site, it will not find any.

### What do I do if a visitor exercises their rights?

1. The visitor contacts you, as controller.
2. Explain the processing to them using the text of this template.
3. It will normally not be possible to locate their specific data, because the identifier is ephemeral (Art. 11 GDPR). But if they provide a piece of data that appears in your conversions (for example, an order number you send as a property), Sealmetrics can help you search for it and delete it.
4. If you need support, write to privacy@sealmetrics.com (clause 4.4 of the DPA).

### Can I send my buyers' email or ID as a conversion property?

**No.** The DPA (clause 5.2) prohibits it. Use data that does not identify individuals: SKU, category, number of items.
